blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Unit 11 (Trigonometric Functions and their Graphs), arranged by the unit's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation that shows the working.
11.1 Domains and Ranges of Sine and Cosine Functions

blocks.prompt: 1 The domain of the function \(\sin\theta\) is:
blocks.explanation: For every real \(\theta\) the terminal side meets the unit circle at exactly one point, so \(\sin\theta = y\) always exists: the domain is \(\mathbb{R}\). \([-1, 1]\) is the range.

book_ref.quote: there is one and only one value of each

blocks.prompt: 2 The range of \(\cos\theta\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(P(x, y)\) is on the unit circle, so \(-1 \le x \le 1\), i.e. \(-1 \le \cos\theta \le 1\); the end values are reached (\(\cos 0 = 1\), \(\cos\pi = -1\)), so square brackets.

book_ref.quote: Thus, the range of sine and cosine functions is

blocks.prompt: 3 Which of the following equations has no solution?
blocks.explanation: The range of sine is \([-1, 1]\) and \(1.2\) lies outside it. \(\cos\theta = -1\) at \(\theta = \pi\), \(\sin\theta = 0.5\) at \(\frac{\pi}{6}\), \(\cos\theta = 0\) at \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).

book_ref.quote: Use the range to spot impossible equations at once.

blocks.prompt: 4 If \(P(x, y)\) is the point where the terminal side of \(\theta\) meets the unit circle, then \(\sin\theta\) equals:
blocks.explanation: With \(OP = 1\): \(\sin\theta = \frac{MP}{OP} = \frac{y}{1} = y\) (and \(\cos\theta = x\)).

book_ref.quote: Unit circle means a circle of radius 1.

blocks.prompt: 5 The smallest value of \(\sin\theta\) and the first angle in \([0, 2\pi]\) where it occurs are:
blocks.explanation: \(-1 \le \sin\theta \le 1\); \(\sin\theta = y = -1\) at the point \(D(0, -1)\), i.e. \(\theta = \frac{3\pi}{2}\). (At \(\pi\), \(\cos\theta = -1\), not \(\sin\theta\).)

book_ref.quote: Every point of the unit circle satisfies

blocks.text: 11.1.1 Domains and Ranges of Tangent and Cotangent Functions

blocks.prompt: 6 \(\tan\theta\) is undefined when \(\theta\) equals:
blocks.explanation: \(\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x}\) needs \(x \ne 0\); \(x = 0\) on the \(Y\)-axis, i.e. at odd multiples of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\): \((2n + 1)\frac{\pi}{2}\).

book_ref.quote: A fraction has no value when its denominator is

blocks.prompt: 7 The domain of \(\cot\theta\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\cot\theta = \frac{x}{y}\) needs \(y \ne 0\); \(y = 0\) at \(0, \pm\pi, \pm 2\pi, \ldots\), i.e. \(n\pi\).

book_ref.quote: For cotangent the denominator is

blocks.prompt: 8 The range of \(\tan\theta\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x}\) is the slope of \(OP\); it takes every real value, so the range is \(\mathbb{R}\). Tangent is not bounded.

book_ref.quote: there is no upper or lower limit

blocks.prompt: 9 At which of these angles is \(\cot\theta\) undefined?
blocks.explanation: Cotangent fails where \(\sin\theta = 0\): \(0^{\circ}, 180^{\circ}, 360^{\circ}, \ldots\) At \(90^{\circ}\) and \(270^{\circ}\), \(\cot\theta = 0\).

book_ref.quote: A quick test: tangent fails where

blocks.prompt: 10 Which of these angles is in the domain of \(\tan\theta\)?
blocks.explanation: The excluded angles are the odd multiples of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\): \(\frac{\pi}{2}, -\frac{3\pi}{2}, \frac{5\pi}{2}\) are all excluded. \(\frac{3\pi}{4}\) is not one of them (\(\tan\frac{3\pi}{4} = -1\)).

book_ref.quote: which is why the short form is

blocks.text: 11.1.2 Domains and Ranges of Secant Function

blocks.prompt: 11 The domain of \(\sec\theta\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\sec\theta = \frac{1}{x}\) needs \(x = \cos\theta \ne 0\): the same condition as tangent.

book_ref.quote: So secant and tangent have the same domain.

blocks.prompt: 12 The range of \(\sec\theta\) is:
blocks.explanation: For \(0 < x \le 1\), \(\frac{1}{x} \ge 1\); for \(-1 \le x < 0\), \(\frac{1}{x} \le -1\). The values \(\pm 1\) are included: \(\sec 0 = 1\), \(\sec\pi = -1\).

book_ref.quote: attains all real values except those between

blocks.prompt: 13 Which of the following can be a value of \(\sec\theta\)?
blocks.explanation: \(|\sec\theta| \ge 1\) for every \(\theta\) in the domain; \(\sec\pi = -1\). The values \(0, 0.5, -0.9\) lie strictly between \(-1\) and \(1\).

book_ref.quote: Remember the shape of the answer

blocks.prompt: 14 If \(\sec\theta = 2\), then \(\cos\theta\) equals:
blocks.explanation: \(\sec\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta}\), so \(\cos\theta = \frac{1}{2}\) (inside \([-1, 1]\), so possible).

book_ref.quote: Secant has the same denominator as tangent

blocks.text: 11.1.3 Domains and Ranges of Cosecant Function

blocks.prompt: 15 The domain of \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta = \frac{1}{y}\) needs \(y = \sin\theta \ne 0\), i.e. \(\theta \ne n\pi\) (including \(\theta = \pi, 3\pi, \ldots\), not only even multiples).

book_ref.quote: so cosecant and cotangent have the same domain

blocks.prompt: 16 The range of \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta \le -1\) or \(\ge 1\); only the open interval \((-1, 1)\) is removed, because \(\operatorname{cosec}\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\) and \(\operatorname{cosec}\frac{3\pi}{2} = -1\).

book_ref.quote: attains all values except those between

blocks.prompt: 17 Which pair of functions has the same domain?
blocks.explanation: \(\tan x\) and \(\sec x\) both have the denominator \(\cos x\), so both exclude \((2n + 1)\frac{\pi}{2}\).

book_ref.quote: The table is easy to remember in three pairs

blocks.prompt: 18 Which number is NOT a value of \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta\)?
blocks.explanation: \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta = \frac{1}{3}\) would need \(\sin\theta = 3\), outside \([-1, 1]\). \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta = 3\) needs \(\sin\theta = \frac{1}{3}\), which is possible.

book_ref.quote: Only the open interval \((-1, 1)\) is removed

blocks.prompt: 19 A function \(f\) is even if, for every \(x\) in its domain:
blocks.explanation: Even: \(f(-x) = f(x)\); odd: \(f(-x) = -f(x)\). \(f(x + 2\pi) = f(x)\) is about periodicity.

book_ref.quote: A function \(f\) is said to be even if

blocks.prompt: 20 The graph of an odd function is always symmetric about:
blocks.explanation: Odd: \((x, f(x))\) and \((-x, -f(x))\) are both on the graph, so it is symmetric about the origin. Even functions are symmetric about the \(y\)-axis.

book_ref.quote: The graph of an odd function is always symmetric about the origin.

blocks.prompt: 21 Which of the following is an even function?
blocks.explanation: \(\cos(-x) = \cos x\), so cosine is even; \(\sin(-x) = -\sin x\), \(\tan(-x) = -\tan x\), \((-x)^{3} = -x^{3}\) are odd.

book_ref.quote: is an even function (see figure 9.2)

blocks.prompt: 22 The function \(f(x) = x\sin x\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(f(-x) = (-x)\sin(-x) = (-x)(-\sin x) = x\sin x = f(x)\): even.

book_ref.quote: To decide whether a function is even, odd or neither

blocks.prompt: 23 The function \(f(x) = \sin x\cos x\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(f(-x) = \sin(-x)\cos(-x) = (-\sin x)(\cos x) = -f(x)\): odd.

book_ref.quote: Odd means: changing the sign of the input changes only the sign of the output.

blocks.prompt: 24 The function \(f(x) = x + \cos x\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(f(-x) = -x + \cos x\). This is not \(f(x) = x + \cos x\) and not \(-f(x) = -x - \cos x\) (e.g. \(x = \pi\): \(f(\pi) = \pi - 1\), \(f(-\pi) = -\pi - 1\)). So neither.

book_ref.quote: Most functions are neither.

blocks.prompt: 25 For a function to be tested for even or odd, its domain must have the property:

options.text: whenever \(x\) is in the domain, \(-x\) is also in it
the domain must be all real numbers
the domain must contain only positive numbers
the domain must be a bounded interval

blocks.explanation: The tests compare \(f(x)\) with \(f(-x)\), so \(-x\) must be in the domain whenever \(x\) is (the domain is symmetric about \(0\)). It need not be all of \(\mathbb{R}\), e.g. \(\tan x\).

book_ref.quote: must also be in the domain of

blocks.prompt: 26 The period of \(\tan\theta\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\tan(\theta + \pi) = \frac{-\sin\theta}{-\cos\theta} = \tan\theta\), and \(\pi\) is the least such positive number. \(2\pi\) also repeats it but is not the least.

book_ref.quote: Tangent is a periodic function and its period is

blocks.prompt: 27 The period of \(\sin 4x\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\sin(4x + 2\pi) = \sin 4\left(x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) = \sin 4x\), so the values repeat when \(x\) increases by \(\frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\).

book_ref.quote: rewrite the shifted angle

blocks.prompt: 28 The period of \(\cot 3x\) is:
blocks.explanation: The period of \(\cot\) is \(\pi\), so \(\cot 3x\) has period \(\frac{\pi}{|3|} = \frac{\pi}{3}\).

book_ref.quote: A quick rule that follows from Example 1

blocks.prompt: 29 The period of \(5 + \cos\frac{x}{4}\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\cos\left(\frac{x}{4} + 2\pi\right) = \cos\frac{1}{4}(x + 8\pi)\); the constant 5 does not change the period: \(\frac{2\pi}{1/4} = 8\pi\).

book_ref.quote: Adding a constant does not change the period.

blocks.prompt: 30 A function \(f\) has period \(p\) if \(f(\theta + p) = f(\theta)\) for all \(\theta\) in its domain and \(p\) is:
blocks.explanation: The period is the least positive \(p\) with \(f(\theta + p) = f(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\); e.g. \(2\pi, 4\pi, 6\pi\) all repeat sine, but its period is \(2\pi\).

book_ref.quote: and the least positive value of

blocks.prompt: 31 \(\pi\) is not the period of \(\sin\theta\) because:
blocks.explanation: Half a turn changes the sign of sine: \(\sin(\pi + \theta) = -\sin\theta\); e.g. \(\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\) but \(\sin\frac{3\pi}{2} = -1\).

book_ref.quote: One counter-example is enough to reject

blocks.prompt: 32 The period of \(\sec\theta\) is:
blocks.explanation: The periods of \(\cos\theta\), \(\csc\theta\) and \(\sec\theta\) are \(2\pi\); those of \(\tan\theta\), \(\cot\theta\) are \(\pi\).

book_ref.quote: By adopting the procedure used in finding the periods of sine and tangent

blocks.prompt: 33 The period of \(\cos\frac{2x}{3}\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\frac{2\pi}{2/3} = 3\pi\). Check: \(\cos\frac{2}{3}(x + 3\pi) = \cos\left(\frac{2x}{3} + 2\pi\right) = \cos\frac{2x}{3}\).

book_ref.quote: runs twice as fast, so the period is halved

blocks.prompt: 34 \(\sin 210^{\circ}\) equals:
blocks.explanation: \(\sin(180^{\circ} + 30^{\circ}) = -\sin 30^{\circ} = -\frac{1}{2}\) (Quadrant III, sine negative).

book_ref.quote: where only tangent is positive

blocks.prompt: 35 \(\cos 300^{\circ}\) equals:
blocks.explanation: \(\cos(360^{\circ} - 60^{\circ}) = \cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\) (Quadrant IV, cosine positive).

book_ref.quote: where only cosine is positive

blocks.prompt: 36 \(\tan 135^{\circ}\) equals:
blocks.explanation: \(\tan(180^{\circ} - 45^{\circ}) = -\tan 45^{\circ} = -1\) (Quadrant II, tangent negative).

book_ref.quote: where only sine is positive

blocks.prompt: 37 \(\cos(-120^{\circ})\) equals:

book_ref.quote: Forgetting the outer minus sign for negative angles

blocks.prompt: 38 \(\sin(-225^{\circ})\) equals:

book_ref.quote: two minus signs make a plus

blocks.prompt: 39 \(\tan 330^{\circ}\) equals:
blocks.explanation: \(\tan(360^{\circ} - 30^{\circ}) = -\tan 30^{\circ} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) (Quadrant IV, tangent negative).

book_ref.quote: The sign follows the quadrant of the angle.

blocks.prompt: 40 \(\cos(\pi - \theta)\) equals:
blocks.explanation: For acute \(\theta\), \(\pi - \theta\) is in Quadrant II where cosine is negative; the name stays the same: \(\cos(\pi - \theta) = -\cos\theta\).

book_ref.quote: the cosine of an angle in Quadrant II is negative

blocks.prompt: 41 In drawing the graph of a trigonometric function, the measures of the angles are taken along:
blocks.explanation: Angles go along the \(X\)-axis and the values of the function along the \(Y\)-axis.

book_ref.quote: The measures of the angles are taken along the

blocks.prompt: 42 The plotted points of a trigonometric graph are joined by:

options.text: straight line segments with a ruler

blocks.explanation: The values change gradually between the plotted points, so they are joined freehand with one smooth curve (no sharp corners).

book_ref.quote: These points are joined with the help of smooth curves.

blocks.prompt: 43 The \(X\)-axis mark \(240^{\circ}\) in radians is:

book_ref.quote: every degree mark has a radian name

blocks.text: 11.4.2 Graph of y = sin x from - 2pi to 2pi

blocks.prompt: 44 The maximum value of \(y = \sin x\) occurs at:
blocks.explanation: \(\sin x = 1\) at \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) and every \(2\pi\) after: \(\frac{\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\). At \(\frac{3\pi}{2} + 2n\pi\) is the minimum \(-1\).

book_ref.quote: When asked for the maximum or minimum of

blocks.prompt: 45 In \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\), the graph of \(y = \sin x\) cuts the \(x\)-axis at how many points?
blocks.explanation: Zeros at \(x = n\pi\): \(-2\pi, -\pi, 0, \pi, 2\pi\), i.e. 5 points.

book_ref.quote: exactly where the curve cuts the

blocks.prompt: 46 The \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y = \sin x\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\sin 0 = 0\): the sine graph passes through the origin. (A start at \((0, 1)\) is cosine.)

book_ref.quote: Sine starts at the origin.

blocks.prompt: 47 The graph of \(y = \sin x\) is symmetric about:
blocks.explanation: \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\): sine is odd, so its graph is symmetric about the origin.

book_ref.quote: The sine function is an odd function.

blocks.prompt: 48 The part of the sine graph over one period, \([0, 2\pi]\), is called:
blocks.explanation: The graph in \([0, 2\pi]\) is called a cycle; the full graph repeats this cycle every \(2\pi\).

book_ref.quote: is called a cycle. Since the period of sine function is

blocks.prompt: 49 For \(180^{\circ} < x < 360^{\circ}\), the graph of \(y = \sin x\) lies:
blocks.explanation: Sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV, so the curve is below the \(x\)-axis there (lowest point \(-1\) at \(270^{\circ}\)).

book_ref.quote: The curve is positive in Quadrants I and II and negative in Quadrants III and IV

blocks.text: 11.4.3 Graph of y = cos x from - 2pi to 2pi

blocks.prompt: 50 The minimum value of \(y = \cos x\) and where it occurs are:
blocks.explanation: \(\cos x = -1\) at odd multiples of \(\pi\), e.g. \(\cos 180^{\circ} = -1\). (The book misprints this minimum as 1.)

book_ref.quote: Copying the misprint: the minimum of

blocks.prompt: 51 The \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y = \cos x\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\cos 0 = 1\): the cosine graph starts at its highest point \((0, 1)\).

book_ref.quote: The cosine curve starts at its highest point

blocks.prompt: 52 The \(x\)-intercepts of \(y = \cos x\) are at:
blocks.explanation: \(\cos x = 0\) at \(90^{\circ}, 270^{\circ}, \ldots\), i.e. \(\frac{\pi}{2} + n\pi\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\). \(n\pi\) are the zeros of sine.

book_ref.quote: Putting the zeros of cosine at

blocks.prompt: 53 The graph of \(y = \cos x\) is symmetric about:
blocks.explanation: \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\): cosine is even, so its graph is symmetric about the \(y\)-axis.

book_ref.quote: The cosine function is an even function, as the graph

blocks.prompt: 54 The graph of y = cos x is the graph of y = sin x moved:
blocks.explanation: \(\cos x = \sin(x + 90^{\circ})\): e.g. \(\cos 0^{\circ} = \sin 90^{\circ} = 1\). Adding \(90^{\circ}\) inside moves the graph \(90^{\circ}\) to the left.

book_ref.quote: so the cosine graph is the sine graph moved

blocks.prompt: 55 The amplitude of \(y = \cos x\) is:
blocks.explanation: The peaks are at height \(1\) above the \(x\)-axis: amplitude \(= \frac{1 - (-1)}{2} = 1\).

book_ref.quote: Same shape as sine, moved

blocks.text: 11.4.4 Graph of y = tan x from -pi to pi

blocks.prompt: 56 The vertical asymptotes of the graph of \(y = \tan x\) are the lines:
blocks.explanation: \(\tan x\) is undefined at \(x = (2n + 1)\frac{\pi}{2}\); the curve approaches these vertical lines but never touches them.

book_ref.quote: is called an asymptote and is drawn dashed

blocks.prompt: 57 As \(x\) approaches \(90^{\circ}\) from the right (e.g. \(91^{\circ}\)), \(\tan x\):
blocks.explanation: Just right of \(90^{\circ}\) the angle is in Quadrant II, where tangent is negative, and \(\cos x\) is near 0: \(\tan 91^{\circ} \approx -57.3\), so \(\tan x \to -\infty\).

book_ref.quote: dividing by a very small number gives a very large answer

blocks.prompt: 58 The amplitude of \(y = \tan x\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(\tan x\) has no maximum or minimum value (range \(\mathbb{R}\)), so its amplitude is undefined.

book_ref.quote: The amplitude of tangent function is undefined because it has no maximum or minimum values.

blocks.prompt: 59 The \(x\)-intercepts of \(y = \tan x\) are at:
blocks.explanation: \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = 0\) where \(\sin x = 0\): \(x = n\pi\), including the origin. \((2n + 1)\frac{\pi}{2}\) are the asymptotes.

book_ref.quote: the graph passes through the origin; odd function

blocks.prompt: 60 On every interval between two consecutive asymptotes, \(\tan x\):
blocks.explanation: Each branch rises from left to right: from \(-\infty\) just right of an asymptote to \(+\infty\) just left of the next.

book_ref.quote: Each branch rises from left to right

blocks.text: 11.5 Maximum and Minimum Values of Given Functions of the Type a + b sin theta, a + b cos theta, a + b sin(c theta + d), a + b cos(c theta + d) and reciprocals

blocks.prompt: 61 The maximum value of \(4 + 3\sin x\) is:

book_ref.quote: Thus the maximum value of

blocks.prompt: 62 The minimum value of \(6 - 5\cos 2x\) is:

book_ref.quote: For any question of this section write three things first

blocks.prompt: 63 The amplitude of \(-7 + 2\sin(3x - 1)\) is:
blocks.explanation: Amplitude \(= |b| = 2\); \(a = -7\) is the vertical shift and \(3\) changes the period.

book_ref.quote: the maximum height of the wave measured from its midline

blocks.prompt: 64 The period of \(3 + 2\sin(4\theta + 1)\) is:
blocks.explanation: Period \(= \frac{2\pi}{c} = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\).

book_ref.quote: Period: the period of (i) is equal to

blocks.prompt: 65 The maximum value of \(\dfrac{1}{4 - \cos x}\) is:
blocks.explanation: \(4 - \cos x\) runs from \(3\) to \(5\) (always positive). The reciprocal is largest when the denominator is smallest: \(\frac{1}{3}\).

book_ref.quote: For a positive reciprocal

blocks.prompt: 66 The maximum value of \(2 - 4\cos x\) occurs when:
blocks.explanation: \(b = -4 < 0\), so \(-4\cos x\) is largest when \(\cos x\) is smallest: \(\cos x = -1\) gives \(M = 2 + 4 = 6\).

book_ref.quote: but the conditions printed with them hold only when

blocks.prompt: 67 A sinusoidal function has maximum value 9 and minimum value 1. Its amplitude is:
blocks.explanation: Amplitude \(= \frac{M - m}{2} = \frac{9 - 1}{2} = 4\) (the midline is \(\frac{9 + 1}{2} = 5\)).

book_ref.quote: The value of the amplitude can also be found using the formula

blocks.prompt: 68 In \(f(\theta) = a + b\sin(c\theta + d)\), the midline of the wave is:
blocks.explanation: \(a\) is the vertical shift: it moves the whole graph up or down, and \(y = a\) is the midline.

book_ref.quote: This shift, also known as the vertical displacement

blocks.prompt: 69 Compared with \(y = \sin\theta\), the graph of \(y = \sin(\theta + d)\) with \(d > 0\) is shifted:
blocks.explanation: A positive phase shift \(d\) moves the graph to the left (here \(c = 1\), so the distance is exactly \(d\)).

book_ref.quote: shifts the graph to the left, while a negative

blocks.prompt: 70 A Ferris wheel has radius 20 ft and its lowest point is 3 ft above the ground. The midline (height of the centre) of its height model is:
blocks.explanation: Amplitude = radius = 20; centre height \(a = 3 + 20 = 23\) ft. (The top is \(43\) ft.)

book_ref.quote: the radius gives the amplitude

blocks.prompt: 71 A wheel makes one revolution in 40 seconds. In \(h(t) = a - b\cos(ct)\), the value of \(c\) is:
blocks.explanation: Period \(\frac{2\pi}{c} = 40 \Rightarrow c = \frac{2\pi}{40} = \frac{\pi}{20}\).

book_ref.quote: after one revolution the rider is back at the same height

blocks.prompt: 72 A rider starts at the lowest point of a wheel. Which model fits (a = height of centre, b = radius)?
blocks.explanation: At \(t = 0\): \(a - b\cos 0 = a - b\), the lowest height. \(a + b\cos(ct)\) starts at the top; \(a + b\sin(ct)\) at the midline.

book_ref.quote: Choosing the starting function

blocks.prompt: 73 The water level of a river is \(L(t) = 10 + 3\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}t\right)\) feet, \(t\) in hours. The period of the level is:
blocks.explanation: Period \(= \frac{2\pi}{c} = \frac{2\pi}{\pi/4} = 8\) hours.

book_ref.quote: Every problem follows the same plan

blocks.prompt: 74 A peak is h metres above the still surface of a lake. Its image in the water is:
blocks.explanation: In a reflection in still water, the image is as far below the surface as the object is above it.

book_ref.quote: the image is as far below the water surface as the object is above it

blocks.prompt: 75 For \(h(t) = 30 - 25\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{20}t\right)\) feet, the height at \(t = 20\) s is:
blocks.explanation: \(h(20) = 30 - 25\cos\pi = 30 + 25 = 55\) ft (the top, half a period after the lowest point).

book_ref.quote: Always test your model at
